title: In-and-Out Dribble Series
description: A lane-to-lane series teaching the in-and-out (fake crossover) move, first stationary, then walking, then at game speed.

content.objective: Fake a crossover with the hand and shoulders while the ball stays in the same hand, freezing the defender before attacking.
content.setup: Players line up along the baseline with a ball each, facing half court.
content.organization: Waves of four to six players at a time.
instructions: Stationary: dribble with the right hand and roll the hand over the top of the ball toward the left, then pull it back out.
Walking: take the in-and-out every two steps, staying low.
Jogging: dip the inside shoulder on the 'in', then explode on the 'out'.
Full speed: in-and-out at the free-throw line, the half-court line and the far free-throw line.
Repeat the whole series with the left hand.
coachingPoints: The ball stays outside the knee; only the hand rolls over it.
Sell the fake with the head and shoulders.
Push off the inside foot to go back out.
commonMistakes: Carrying the ball (palm under the ball) on the roll.
Fake too small to move a defender.
content.safety: Keep waves in separate lanes; return along the sideline, not through the next wave.
progressions: Chain the in-and-out into a real crossover (double move).
Add a defender who must react.
regressions: Practise the hand roll without dribbling.
Do the stationary stage only for U10.
variations: Finish each run with a pull-up jump shot.
Use a coach as a passive defender at half court.
successCriteria: Ball never crosses the body during the in-and-out.
No carrying calls in a full series.
content.gameApplication: The in-and-out punishes a defender who jumps at the crossover; it gets the ball handler past the first defender without changing hands.
